summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial: Modifying a T-shirt into a Bunny Girl Outfit ## Introduction Hello everyone! In this tutorial video, we will learn how to modify a T-shirt into an integrated bunny costume. This process will also include the production of stockings. ## Setting Up the Virtual Environment 1. **Importing the Model** First, we need to find the stylized avatar file in the library window. Double-click on Hana to import this virtual model. 2. **Importing the Garment** Next, locate the garment folder, double-click, and then import the T-shirt. Open it by double-clicking again. ## Arranging the T-shirt 3. **Positioning the T-shirt** Press `Shift + F` to open the arrangement point. Click on the sleeve panel, and then click on the arrangement point on the side. After arranging, also adjust the front to the corresponding position. **Note**: Ensure that the garment is centered on the arrangement point to facilitate accurate adjustments. 4. **Avoiding Obstructions** If the sewing line passes through Hana's hair, it may block the panel. Manually move the panel down slightly in 3D space to avoid this issue. ## Simulating and Modifying the Garment 5. **Simulation Control** Press the `Control` key to start the simulation. Press it again to pause. Select the two sleeve panels and delete them, as we're now inserting a male T-shirt that does not match Hana's body shape. 6. **Adjusting Width** The first adjustment is the width of the T-shirt. Use the adjustment panel tool to select one side of the front and back panels. There’s no need to select the other side simultaneously, as modifications on one side will mirror on the other. - Drag the side point of the selection box. While dragging, press the right key to enter a specific value. Set the width to 80%. - Unlock the adjacent level adjustment to modify width and height separately. Restore the height to 100 and click OK. 7. **Finalizing the Simulation** After opening the simulation, you will see how the garment fits Hana. Next, adjust the height for a better fit. ## Refining the Design 8. **Panel Adjustment** To simplify adjustments later, position the panel closer to the cutout in the 2D window. Use the edit panel tool to make necessary adjustments. 9. **Optimizing Sleeve Size** Switch to the side view and notice the sleeves appear too large. Utilize tools in the edit panel tool group for optimization. - Activate the 3D mirror for simultaneous adjustments to both sides. - Select points on the front and back sleeves. Use the `Shift` key to select multiple points. - Move the points vertically, using a pink guide line for reference. Enter a vertical value of 100 and click OK. 10. **Adjusting Surface Diameter** When creating tight clothing, reduce the surface diameter of the virtual model to create a closer fit. This adjustment helps reduce air thickness around the model, making the fabric appear more form-fitting. ## Shoulder Line and Overall Fit 11. **Shoulder Line Importance** The shoulder line is crucial in determining whether clothing looks integrated or loose. For dresses or tighter garments, align the shoulder line based on arm movement. 12. **Adjusting the Skirt Design** If designing a one-piece skirt, adjust the side of the board accordingly. If unsure how much to adjust, switch to a transparent picture view as a reference. ## Drawing Reference Lines 13. **Using 3D Line Drawing** To draw reference lines on the garment, access the 3D line drawing tool group from the toolbar. - Switch to a transparent picture view to see the virtual model's body. - Click on the shoulder position near the bottom of the page, then double-click the back piece to finish the line. 14. **Adjusting the 2D Window** Switch to the edit board tool to adjust the garment in the 2D window, moving points to align with the reference lines drawn. ## Waist Adjustment 15. **Waist Modification** To modify the waist to fit Hana's body shape better, we need to add points at the waist. Enable the transparent picture display and select the back piece for adjustments. - Use the plus point division function by clicking near the thinnest point of the waist (indicated by a blue dot). - Move the waist points inwards using the edit tool, pressing the `Shift` key for horizontal movement. 16. **Final Adjustments** Aim to adjust both the front and back pieces simultaneously. Enter specific values for inward movement (e.g., 30mm for the front waist and the same for the back). - After adjustments, briefly simulate to see the effect. Check for overall fit and make additional modifications as necessary. 17. **Conclusion** When satisfied with the waist adjustment, avoid further modifications that could affect the upper and lower body fit. Instead, focus on refining the overall version of the garment. ```
